---
title: "Counting the observations in each class"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
library(tidyverse)
```

Here's some data (the Wisconsin Breast Cancer data set, originally from the [UCI machine learning repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/17/breast+cancer+wisconsin+diagnostic)) where we would like to calculate the number of observations in each class:

```{r}
#| label: load-data
cancer <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UBC-DSCI/introduction-to-datascience/main/data/wdbc.csv")
cancer
```

To calculate the number of observations of each class, we group the rows by class and count them:

```{r}
#| label: count-classes
cancer |>
  group_by(Class) |>
  summarize(count = n()) |>
  rename(class = Class)
```

We do this for almost every classification problem we work on.
Next, we will move this code into a function, `count_classes`, in `../R/count_classes.R`,
write tests for that function,
and call the function here instead.
